summary.text: Jay Feely is a former NFL placekicker (2001-2014) and CBS football analyst, and the Republican nominee for Arizona's 1st Congressional District, an open seat. He played college football at the University of Michigan and began his congressional campaign in 2025, first in the 5th District and later in the 1st. As of July 1, 2026, he had raised $2.53 million to Amish Shah's $1.83 million.

paragraphs.text: Feely, whose full name is Thomas "Jay" Feely IV, earned a bachelor's degree in finance from the University of Michigan in 1998 and, according to FOX 10 Phoenix, was a member of Michigan's 1997 national championship team.

He worked as a financial advisor before his football career. He then played as a kicker for six NFL teams from 2001 to 2014, including four years with the Arizona Cardinals, and served on the NFLPA Executive Committee for over a decade.
After football, Feely became an NFL analyst for CBS, where FOX 10 Phoenix says he spent a decade and won an Emmy Award, and he served on the Gilbert Christian High School board from 2016 to 2020.
He also serves on corporate boards, works as an angel investor, and runs the Feely Family Foundation with his wife, Rebecca.

Feely announced a run for Congress in 2025 in the 5th District. After President Donald Trump endorsed Mark Lamb in that race, Feely announced on December 19, 2025 that he would run in the 1st District instead.

He won the July 21, 2026 Republican primary with 49.8% of the vote over Joseph Chaplik (35.7%) and John Trobough (14.5%) with Trump's endorsement; FOX 10 Phoenix reports he has faced criticism for living outside the district.
